{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ga-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"11c5a52f8738dc4880a740879d42cd3dd0e7aeaa136a919110b43fc44d45d92c","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ga-class-c:lineage:42","source_registry_sha256":"e082bc406bec2cfadcd011c884a136274a0200b40ae5a1536777a259a1b09eb3","source_liveness_sha256":"899bb7b77ecc9a36dd3203950c0cfa2065e4529a11881605f77eacb7d739a757"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Signals, pedestrian beacons, markings and roundabouts","heading":"Signals, pedestrian beacons, markings and roundabouts","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## Signals, pedestrian beacons, markings and roundabouts

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
Drivers, bicyclists and pedestrians must obey traffic signals unless an officer directs traffic differently. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
When an intersection's ordinary traffic signal is completely inoperative, treat every approach as stop-controlled. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A01
When an ordinary malfunctioning intersection signal flashes, follow its displayed color: flashing yellow calls for caution, while flashing red requires a stop before proceeding safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A01
A steady red traffic light requires stopping before entering the crosswalk or intersection and waiting for green, subject to separately stated permitted red-turn rules. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A01
A steady yellow signal warns that green is ending and red is next; slow and prepare to stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A01
A green signal permits movement only when safe after stopping for pedestrians and yielding to vehicles already in the intersection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A01
A green arrow permits careful travel only in the arrow's direction, after yielding to vehicles in the intersection and stopping for pedestrians. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A01
A yellow arrow following a green arrow warns drivers to clear the intersection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A01
Treat a flashing red traffic light like a stop sign: stop fully, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, then proceed cautiously when safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A01
A flashing yellow traffic light requires slowing and caution before continuing through the junction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A01
A flashing yellow left-turn arrow permits the left turn only after yielding to pedestrians and oncoming vehicles; opposing traffic still has green. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A01
A walk indication permits a pedestrian to leave the curb and begin crossing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A01
A do-not-walk indication tells pedestrians not to begin crossing. During the flashing phase, someone already crossing should finish rather than start from the curb. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A01
Overhead lane-use signs can restrict a lane to a left turn, right turn, or the stated combination of straight and left movement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A02
A pedestrian hybrid beacon is activated by a pedestrian's push button to stop road traffic and provide a walk indication for crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=36]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A02
A pedestrian hybrid beacon normally remains dark until a person activates it; this is the beacon's inactive state rather than an ordinary failed intersection signal. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=36]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A02
After pedestrian activation, the hybrid beacon first displays flashing yellow to approaching traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=36]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A02
The hybrid beacon next changes to steady yellow, advising drivers to slow and prepare for a stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=36]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A02
Double steady red indications at a pedestrian hybrid beacon require drivers to stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=36]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A02
During the following alternating flashing-red phase of the hybrid beacon, each driver must make a complete stop and proceed only after pedestrians have cleared the crosswalk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=36]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A02
After the pedestrian hybrid beacon's crossing cycle ends, it returns to dark until another pedestrian activates it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=36]

Misconceptions: A normally dark pedestrian hybrid beacon and a failed ordinary traffic signal have different meanings; a flashing red indication still requires a complete stop.
Mnemonic: Identify the device, read its phase, yield, then move.
Glossary: A hybrid beacon is a pedestrian-activated control; a center turn lane serves left turns from either direction; a refuge divides a pedestrian crossing into stages.
Dynamic-fact isolation: Graphic interpretation, current marking standards and visual asset rights remain separately reviewed; artwork is not reconstructed from garbled extraction.
